source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

hinge.title: Decide whether a rectangular grid can be tiled by 2 x 1 tiles using area parity and an explicit row-or-column strategy.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Unit squares is the label that belongs on this item, so 'Decide whether a rectangular grid can be tiled by 2 x 1 tiles using' is answered as unit squares rather than m x n grid.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: m x n grid still holds here even though The region must be a rectangular grid of unit squares for the row-or-column strategy is missing from the stem — on the item about Decide whether a rectangular grid can be tiled by 2 x 1.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Even row or column count supplies a complete tiling strategy is what produces grid dimensions determine total unit squares and available row or column pairings, so the usual direction of this relation is run backwards — on the item about Decide whether a rectangular grid can be tiled by 2 x 1.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The m x n grid rule also covers this: regions with missing squares, so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide whether a rectangular grid can be tiled by 2 x 1.

intelligence.enrichment: A 2 x 1 tile covers exactly two unit squares. A rectangular grid with an odd number of unit squares cannot be tiled by such tiles; when a rectangle has an even number of rows or columns, it can be tiled by filling columns or rows with rotated copies.
